## 7 changes: dall-e-2/dall-e-3 and Realtime beta header removed May 12, 2026; realtime preview/audio-preview models May 7, 2026 and more [Verified]

Realtime: model is now gpt-realtime-2.1 (URL constant exported), OpenAI-Beta header removed, session.update uses the GA shape (type realtime, audio formats pcm 24k, voice under audio.output), handler listens for response.output_audio.delta. gpt-4o-realtime-preview and the Realtime beta header are already removed. The gpt-4o-mini default shuts down 2027-01-14, which is within 90 days.

> On November 14th, 2025, we notified developers using DALL·E model snapshots of their deprecation and removal from the API on May 12, 2026.

review.summary: The Realtime GA migration (URL, header removal, session shape, event rename) is coherent and covered by a new spec, which is the one check that flipped fail to pass. The chat.completions side is much weaker. Every default model was changed to 'gpt-6-luna', which I could not confirm exists. Nothing in the quoted source (a DALL·E removal notice) mentions it, and the checks never call the API. Several sites also gained behaviour changes (temperature removed, max_tokens renamed) that go beyond what the quoted deprecation forces. 'gpt-realtime-2.1' is likewise unconfirmed. Marking this 'verified' overstates what the checks prove. Pre-existing: the repo has no DALL·E usage in the shown call sites, so the headline deprecation may not apply here.

concerns.issue: Default model changed from gpt-4o-mini to 'gpt-6-luna' across all chat.completions sites (ai.service, dispatch-email, task-assignment, notification/suggestion clients, market-intelligence, meeting.service x4, proposal-plan). I could not confirm this model ID from the quoted source. If it is wrong, every OpenAI call fails at runtime, and several callers swallow errors into fallback text (ai.service returns an apology), so the failure would be silent. No test hits the API.

Model 'gpt-realtime-2.1' and the new session.update shape (type:'realtime', output_modalities, audio.input/output format with rate) are unconfirmed against the quoted source. The spec only asserts the code matches itself with a mocked ws, so a real handshake is unproven. The input format object ({type:'audio/pcm', rate:24000}) should be checked against the SDK types.

Removed temperature (0.15) and renamed max_tokens to max_completion_tokens. The JSON-assignment output was tuned for low temperature, so dropping it makes assignments less deterministic. This is a behaviour change not forced by the quoted deprecation, perhaps justified by the new model rejecting temperature, but that is not shown.

Same temperature removal (0.2) and token-param rename in dispatch-email and proposal-plan-generator. The plan generator parses JSON output, so higher variance may increase parse failures. These changes are applied only to some call sites, while ai.service and meeting.service pass no such params, so the treatment is inconsistent.

The relay still forwards response.output_text.delta, but the GA text event name may differ (e.g. response.output_text.delta vs the audio transcript events). The diff only renames the audio delta. The docs also tell clients that the event now arrives as response.output_audio.delta, which is a breaking contract change for the Flutter client that the PR does not flag.

Docs and .env.example now advertise gpt-6-luna as default, and the removal of the gpt-4o option from the docs table limits users' fallback choices. Existing deployments with OPENAI_MODEL set in env are unaffected, but those relying on the default will switch models silently.

Check whether the Flutter client depends on response.audio.delta and needs a coordinated update.
Confirm whether removing temperature was required by the new model or an unrequested change; consider restoring it if the model accepts it.
